claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.

Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories so that each repository contains exactly one package, grouping cohesive components within it, and using multiple repositories (one per package) for distinct packages.
The version of a source-based plugin package is the Git tag on its repository.
Source-based plugin packages are distributed as source code in a Git repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag (e.g., v1.2.3) to the repository, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Publishing to the Private Registry is typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

Executable-based plugin packages are distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Pulumi IDP has a Private Registry documented at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/.

Linked pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/packages/, /docs/iac/concepts/components/, packaging-components anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages, /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/, /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/, and /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that conflicts with how Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected, and they ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with the supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The Amazon EKS package's components are almost always used together and tend to evolve together, so a shared semantic version makes sense.
One `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.

A package repository layout with `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the root and components in a `components/` directory (e.g., components/EksCluster/, components/EksIam/) is a valid structure for a Pulumi package.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, though it is technically possible.
Semantic versioning is how consumers know whether a given change is a bug fix, a new feature, or a breaking change.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.

In a package containing ComponentA and ComponentB, an enhancement to ComponentA yields a v1.1.0 release and a breaking change to ComponentB yields a v2.0.0 release (semver minor and major bumps respectively), even though ComponentA and ComponentB are unchanged by the other's change.
